description: Two triangle oscillators that modulate each other and clock two shift registers, whose stepped output modulates them back and drives a twin-peak resonant filter

params.text: Sets the base frequency of oscillator A, from about 0.03Hz at the bottom of its travel to about 11000Hz at the top
Sets the base frequency of oscillator B, from about 0.03Hz at the bottom of its travel to about 11000Hz at the top
Sets the resonance of the two peaks in the filter
Sets how far oscillator B modulates the frequency of oscillator A
Sets how far oscillator A modulates the frequency of oscillator B
Sets how far the sample-and-hold moves both oscillator frequencies
Sets how far the rungler moves oscillator A, which is one half of the feedback that makes the module chaotic
Sets how far the rungler moves oscillator B, which is the other half of that feedback
Sets how far the sample-and-hold pushes the two filter peaks apart and together
Sets the base cutoff of the first filter peak, 20Hz to 20000Hz
Sets the base cutoff of the second filter peak, 20Hz to 20000Hz
Sets how far the rungler moves both filter peaks

inputs.text: Transposes oscillator A, one volt per octave
Transposes oscillator B, one volt per octave
Transposes the first filter peak, one volt per octave
Transposes the second filter peak, one volt per octave

outputs.text: The two runglers added together as a stepped voltage, 0V to 10V, for driving the rest of the rack from the module's own pattern

notes: this plays itself and there is deliberately no way to play a melody on it: no gate jack, no envelope, nothing to sequence notes into.
the twin-peak filter is two resonant low-passes fed in opposite phase and summed, which leaves a resonant band between the two peaks.
the four pitch jacks are an addition of this module; the circuit it is modelled on has no inputs at all.
